key_numbers.metric: Pass Rate, function body (GPT-3.5-Turbo, all repos)

key_numbers.value: K=10 max snippets; window Sw=20/50, Ss=10

budget_tradeoff_detail: Retrieval budget (K=10 snippets, fixed window sizes) held constant across RepoCoder iterations/Oracle; no explicit token-cost-vs-quality sweep reported beyond fixed prompt/generation token caps (4096/2048).
confound_note: In-File vs RepoCoder varies both the presence of retrieval and its content (no cross-file budget at all vs a fixed K=10 retrieval budget); the more controlled contrast (Iter-1/Iter-2 vs Oracle) holds K and window sizes constant while varying only query quality (self-predicted vs ground-truth continuation).
stop_detail: Iteratively retrieves up to K=10 sliding-window code snippets via sparse Jaccard similarity, using the model's own draft prediction to refine the next round's retrieval query, then concatenates retrieved snippets with local context into the prompt (Sec 2.1-2.3).
threats_to_datum: Benchmark repos are Python-only, small-to-medium (157-443 files) and curated post-training-cutoff; generalization to larger repos or other languages untested.

demote_reason: Full text shows ToolGen has no repository-level context representation or token/context budget at all: it fine-tunes the LLM to emit a special trigger token that invokes the Jedi IDE autocompletion tool for single-identifier suggestions via live static scope analysis, with no explicit context window or structural retrieval of cross-file content managed by the method (Sec II-B, III-B/C). It substitutes a tool call for context expansion rather than engaging any cross-file structural-budget problem, so it falls outside the study's scope.

budget_tradeoff_detail: Half of total input length is pre-allocated to background knowledge and half to unfinished code by design; DraCo is ~100x faster at prompt construction than RepoCoder while also improving accuracy, but context sizes/snippet counts are not equalized across baselines (Table 5).
confound_note: DraCo vs RepoCoder varies both representation/mechanism (dataflow-graph-guided entity retrieval vs sliding-window similarity retrieval) and the effective context budget (different snippet-count limits per method: unrestricted graph-derived entities vs RepoCoder's fixed K), so budget is not held constant in the central comparison.
stop_detail: Parses the repository into a typed dataflow graph (entities linked by assigns/refers/typeof/inherits relations), then given unfinished code, extracts its imports and retrieves connected entities via depth-first search, restoring them to source text concatenated into the prompt (Sec 3.2-3.4).
threats_to_datum: Python-only; retrieval precision depends on import/name-matching heuristics that may not generalize to dynamically-typed or reflection-heavy code patterns.

key_numbers.metric: Avg. prompt tokens per context level

budget_tradeoff_detail: Full context (362.9 avg tokens) vs Medium (253.1) vs Small (179.7) trades token budget for representational completeness (full body vs signature+docstring vs signature-only); richer/costlier context generally raises both Pass@1 and DIR (Table 4).
confound_note: The central Full/Medium/Small ablation varies token budget AND representational completeness simultaneously by construction (removing docstrings/bodies both shrinks tokens and removes information), so budget and content richness are confounded, not isolated.
stop_detail: A custom static-analysis tool (`pydepcall`) uses tree-sitter ASTs and a call graph to identify cross-file dependencies, which are rendered at one of three fixed granularities (full implementation / signature+docstring / signature-only) and concatenated into the generation prompt (Sec 3).
threats_to_datum: Python-only, 355 samples; only 22.8% of tasks involve cross-file dependencies; DIR metric and LLM-generated test cases carry their own coverage/noise limitations.

key_numbers.metric: Soft Exact Match, CKG symbol definition (struct init)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Context capped at 4k-8k input tokens with only top-2 to top-4 retrieved snippets per source; the larger 8k budget boosts similar-code SEM more than 4k (Table III), but no full budget-vs-quality curve is swept.
confound_note: Each of the three context types (user behavior, similar code, symbol definitions) is ablated independently against a no-context baseline, so mechanism/representation and presence-vs-absence of that source vary together; token budget is fixed within an ablation but differs across the 4k-vs-8k comparison.
stop_detail: Combines three retrieval channels at completion time-recently-browsed-file snippets ranked by cursor-click interaction, Jaccard-similarity code snippets from an inverted index, and symbol/struct definitions from a proprietary Code Knowledge Graph built via incremental static analysis-concatenated into an up-to-8k-token prompt (Sec III-A/B/C).
threats_to_datum: Offline benchmarks are internal/proprietary and not publicly released; production A/B improvements are self-reported by the industrial (ByteDance) team without external replication.

demote_reason: Full text confirms this operates at single-file granularity only: 'prompts are constructed per-file' from SonarQube findings, with no cross-file context aggregation, no structural repository representation, and no token/context-budget management across the codebase (Sec III-A2, IV-A5). Its RAG component retrieves external fix suggestions from GitHub/StackOverflow/Google, not repository-internal structural context, so there is no cross-file structural-budget concern for this study.

key_numbers.metric: Token cost of agentic frameworks vs direct prompting

budget_tradeoff_detail: Agentic frameworks (SWE-agent/OpenHands) substantially raise QA quality over direct prompting or sliding-window RAG but consume roughly 100x more tokens (Table 8), a steep token-cost-for-accuracy tradeoff with no budget normalization across methods.
confound_note: Comparison across direct prompting, sliding-window RAG, function-chunking RAG, AST-based retrieval, and agentic exploration varies representation/mechanism and token/context budget simultaneously (agentic methods use ~100x more tokens), so accuracy gains cannot be attributed to representation alone.
stop_detail: Compares four context strategies for repository QA-fixed raw sliding-window chunks (500 lines/100 overlap), embedding-based function-chunk retrieval (voyage-code-3, K=10), a tree-sitter-derived typed AST graph, and agentic exploration (OpenHands/SWE-agent tool-use loops, max 10 iterations) (Sec 3.1-3.2).
threats_to_datum: Scored via LLM-as-judge (Claude Sonnet 4.5) with only limited human validation (3 engineers, 50 questions); the full-text version fetched reports 720 QA pairs across 15 repositories, whereas the abstract supplied for this record states 576 pairs/11 repos-likely a v1-vs-v2 numbers drift that should be reconciled against the exact arXiv version cited.

key_numbers.metric: RepoExec Exact Match, relative gain over strongest baseline

budget_tradeoff_detail: Backbone LLM context windows (DeepSeek-V3 128K, Qwen3-Coder 262K, GPT-5-mini 400K) are used as-is with no explicit token-budget-vs-quality sweep reported; gains are reported only as relative EM/BLEU improvements over baselines (Sec 4.4, 5.1).
confound_note: Comparison to RAG baselines varies both representation (bidirectional call-graph inlining vs retrieved snippets) and effective prompt content/length, with no matched token budget across methods or across the three differently-sized backbone context windows.
stop_detail: Generates a draft anchor for the target function, then inlines it into its caller (upstream: parameter substitution, return normalization, inline expansion) and retrieves callee implementations via AST parsing plus substring matching (downstream), producing one linearized function-scope context (Sec 3.3).
threats_to_datum: Python-only benchmarks (DevEval, RepoExec); downstream callee retrieval relies on LLM-predicted names plus substring matching, which may mismatch in large or ambiguous namespaces.

budget_tradeoff_detail: none precisely reported - context window sizes differ by underlying model/agent but are not standardized or swept as an explicit token-budget variable.
confound_note: Cross-agent comparison (mini-SWE-agent vs SWE-agent vs OpenHands vs Agentless vs Prometheus) varies representation/mechanism (shell exploration vs embedding retrieval vs graph-based navigation) and the underlying LLM simultaneously, with no budget control.
stop_detail: Instruments agent trajectories during issue resolution to record every accessed file/line/block, then scores retrieved context against human-annotated gold contexts at file/block/line granularity for recall, precision, F1, redundancy, and usage-drop (Sec 2.5, 3.4).
threats_to_datum: Not yet peer-reviewed (Feb 2026 preprint); human-curated gold-context annotations may not capture all valid solution paths, biasing recall/precision estimates.

benchmarks: BMW industrial DSL dataset (774 train / 105 held-out)
budget_tradeoff_detail: none reported precisely - paper states both 7B models had 'adequate context to include instruction, full linearized project context, and generate the fully updated JSON without truncation,' so no token-budget-vs-quality curve is quantified.
confound_note: Zero-shot/Raw vs one-shot ICL vs fine-tuned arms all receive the same full, untruncated linearized-JSON project context, varying only the adaptation/prompting mechanism-a relatively clean mechanism-only ablation at a fixed (effectively unconstrained) context budget.
stop_detail: Encodes the entire DSL project folder hierarchy as one nested JSON document (folders as objects, files as keys, contents as string values) and feeds the full linearized project state plus instruction as a single prompt, generating a complete updated JSON in one response (Sec 4.1).
threats_to_datum: Small held-out set (105 examples) from a single company/DSL, modest average scope (~6.1 files, ~196 LOC context); by construction the paper sidesteps the structural-budget problem this SLR studies since everything always fits without truncation, limiting relevance to larger repos.

benchmarks: 2 production SDK case studies (no named public benchmark)

key_numbers.metric: Input tokens, tutorial validation case study
Wall-clock time, tutorial validation case study

budget_tradeoff_detail: CAIS reduces both wall-clock time (22-34%) and input tokens (16-32%) relative to the baseline agent with ordinary repo tools, while surfacing more issues (13 vs 5) - no quality-for-budget tradeoff observed; both cost and quality improved together (Tables 3-4).
confound_note: Baseline vs baseline+CAIS varies both the retrieval mechanism (ordinary file-read/keyword/symbol tools vs a hybrid BM25+dense fused index) and the resulting token budget (CAIS used fewer tokens), so representation and effective budget move together rather than being held constant.
stop_detail: Indexes source code, API references, and docs with combined BM25 lexical search plus DRAMA dense embeddings, fused via reciprocal rank fusion; the documentation agent issues tool-call queries against this index within its task loop to trace cross-file evidence chains (Sec 3.2-3.3).
threats_to_datum: Only 2 case studies on a single production SDK (~200 files) with one agent/model (Claude Sonnet 4.6); not peer-reviewed; the documentation-generation/validation task is adjacent to the core code-generation focus of most other records in this review.

key_numbers.metric: Pass@2, average gain over baseline agents

key_numbers.value: WebDesignIter 33.53% Pass@1 @533K tokens vs Claude Code 21.27% @13,949K tokens

budget_tradeoff_detail: WebDesignIter achieves higher Pass@1 (33.53% vs 21.27%) than Claude Code while using ~26x fewer input tokens (533K vs 13,949K) (Table 4, RQ4) - its structured KG retrieval is both cheaper and more accurate than general-purpose agentic exploration.
confound_note: The headline WebDesignIter-vs-Claude-Code comparison varies representation/mechanism (persistent architecture-KG retrieval vs general agentic file exploration) and token budget simultaneously (~26x difference), so accuracy and efficiency gains are confounded rather than isolated; the design-knowledge ablation (Table 2) does not report matched token budgets either.
stop_detail: Maintains a persistent 'WebAppArchKG' knowledge graph-built from Tree-sitter ASTs, file-level import dependencies, and design/architecture annotations-kept in sync across development cycles; planning and generation stages retrieve nodes connected via relevant edges and apply diff-based patches validated in a sandbox (Sec I: A-C).
threats_to_datum: Not peer-reviewed (preprint); evaluated only on Web-Bench (Vue/Angular/Tailwind front-end projects), so generalization to other stacks or backend code is untested.

key_numbers.value: up to 52.1% vs RAG; 47.6% vs RepoFormer

budget_tradeoff_detail: MRCoder improves Pass@1 by 52.7% relative (36.5% vs 23.9%, CoderEval K=10) while simultaneously cutting token consumption 30-50% and inference time up to 52.1% versus plain RAG-reporting simultaneous cost and quality gains rather than a tradeoff curve (Table 2, Sec 5.1-5.2).
confound_note: MRCoder vs RAG/RepoFormer baselines varies both the context-selection mechanism (map-reduce draft-guided filtering vs plain top-K similarity retrieval) and the resulting token budget (MRCoder uses fewer tokens), so quality gains are not isolated from the budget reduction-both move together in MRCoder's favor.
stop_detail: Map phase partitions retrieved candidates into fixed-size groups, has a lightweight LLM draft code per group, then Structure-Aware Draft-Guided Selection keeps contexts whose APIs match the draft's calls (API-Call Perspective) or whose BM25 similarity to the draft is high (Logic Similarity Perspective); Reduce phase feeds the filtered union to a larger target LLM with parallel/speculative verification decoding (Sec 3.2-3.4).
threats_to_datum: Not yet peer-reviewed (under TOSEM review); CoderEval Python subset is small (230 tasks); draft-quality dependency means errors in the lightweight draft model could bias the API-match filtering.
